title: Daylight traffic garden playpad and release notes (sketch)
content:
Context and intent:
This is a working "playpad" for a daylight-forward mini-launch (regional weekday midday window) where traffic warmup is the primary risk. Goal is to provide: 1) an hourly sentinel grid for the day-of team, 2) a compact traffic shaping guide (the "garden"), 3) release notes draft (customer-visible) and 4) clear rollback & escalation triggers.

Top-level constraints/assumptions:
- Midday window (14:00–18:00 PT) to avoid overnight on-call pain.
- Target cohort: 5% of traffic to start, 20% by 3h if stable.
- Observability: route-level latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, token cost per request, cold-starts, and KV-hit ratio must be visible in the console.
- Canary model variant: rwd-model-v2-quant (cpu-fallback enabled).

Day-of hourly sentinel grid (compact):
- T-minus 60m: final preflight (smoke tests on staging, DB migrations dry-run, quota checks). Owner: Miguel.
- T-minus 30m: announce launch on #release-ops and pager channel; ensure backout binaries staged. Owner: Priya.
- T-plus 0m: route 0.5% traffic. Verify p50 < target, errors < 0.1%. Owner: Aisha.
- T-plus 15m: if stable, route 2%. Check KV cache hit, batching stats; snapshot logs.
- T-plus 45m: escalate to 5% if metrics OK. Run light load test (10k qps burst simulation).
- T-plus 120m: target 10–20% depending on rate-limiting thresholds. Confirm per-route cost delta < +15%.
- T-plus 4h: complete ramp to target cohort and transition to steady state watch.

Traffic garden (shaping heuristics) — the short recipe:
- Start with narrow ingress lanes: regionally scoped prefixes only.
- Enforce per-route token cap (soft throttle) at 1.5x baseline to protect bursty clients.
- Autoscaler policy: scale-up aggressive (10s), scale-down conservative (5m).
- KV/Prefix cache warmup: pin common prefixes for first 30m if possible.
- Batching: enable continuous batching but cap batch size to avoid large latency tail for short prompts.
- Fallback model lanes: rwd-model-v2-quant -> rwd-model-v2-fp16 -> cpu-fallback; use costs/lantency policy for routing.

Launch checklist (short):
- [ ] Release notes draft reviewed by docs (link below)
- [ ] Canary variant baked and verified against smoke prompts
- [ ] Backout toggle exists and tested (rollback route + model pin)
- [ ] On-call rota confirmed for next 48h with handoff times
- [ ] Billing/Quota guardrails set (hard stop at X tokens/min)
- [ ] Alert runbook updated with new signal thresholds

Quick rollback decision matrix (field guide):
- Immediate rollback (auto): error rate spike > 2% sustained 5m OR p99 latency > 4x baseline 10m
- Manual rollback: token cost delta > 40% over 30m OR widespread client 4xx/5xx patterns tied to new variant
- Throttle-only: low-volume behavioral regressions, minor quality drop, or batch-queue buildup.

Communication templates (short):
- Slack (to #release-ops): "LAUNCH UPDATE: routing 2% -> rwd-model-v2-quant. Watching p50/p95/p99 and error_rate. Oncall: Priya/Aisha. Escalate to @Miguel if errors > 0.5%."
- Customer-facing release note blurb (draft): "We rolled out performance and cost improvements to our text-generation endpoint (rwd-model-v2-quant). Expect faster median latency and lower unit cost. If you see any change in output quality for high-sensitivity prompts, please contact support@redwood.ai and include your request id."

Observability quick hits (what to watch first):
1) per-route error-rate and top-5 error messages
2) p99 latency and latency distribution shifts
3) KV cache hit ratio (if drops, quality/cost may be impacted)
4) Token-per-request moving average
5) Autoscaler thrash (frequent up/down cycles)

Open questions / followups (to resolve before final):
- Do we want to expose the per-route hard-stop tokens/min to customers or keep as internal guard? (Decision needed from product).
- Confirm whether the billing guard should be per-org or global for this daylight window.
- Need docs sign-off on the customer blurb by EOD before launch.

Links / attachments / references:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-RELEASE-824 (detailed preflight)
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-4123 (canary bake tasks)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1987 (autoscaler tweak)
